Method of Attack: STONESTOP is a user-mode application that attempts to terminate endpoint security software processes on a device and acts as a loader/installer for POORTRY driver.
POORTRY is a kernel-mode driver signed by Microsoft used to terminate protected security software processes or Windows services.
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with kernel-mode driver support
Telecommunication, BPO, MSSP, financial services businesses
Medical industry companies targeted by Hive ransomware
Systems compromised by Cuba ransomware operation
Systems targeted by UNC3944 threat group
Attack Vector: Malicious kernel-mode hardware drivers signed via Microsoft's Windows Hardware Developer Program
Post-exploitation activity after attackers gained administrative privileges
Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks
Indicators of Compromise: Suspended Microsoft Partner Center developer accounts
Microsoft Defender signatures 1.377.987.0 to detect signed drivers in post-exploitation
